answer: Randomized Mirror Slot Assignment. Each round, a verifiable random function run over a public beacon assigns each identity a slot; an identity only earns if it also mirrors a randomly chosen counterpart's recent signed work. Because the target is drawn after commit, attackers cannot precompute which colluding identities pair up. Scaling to N identities costs N full work submissions per round, so forging K convincing nodes multiplies real compute and storage K-fold with no shortcut; the short horizon before reslotting denies any stable oasis of prearranged pairs.
